Part 2 introduces the case, because every line of R that you write today works on its data, then the place where R is written and R itself, from assigning a value to drawing a plot. The part takes ninety minutes, and the last half hour is yours.

## 1. The paper

**On the slides.** The slides present the paper of the original authors (OAs): the question that it asks, the design, the email word for word, what came back for each of the six names, and the four outcomes that were coded. They end on the claim as SCORE selected it.

## 2. The IDE

**On the slides.** The slides show the four places of an IDE that are worth knowing, why you open the folder of the workspace rather than a single file, and the different jobs of the console and the script. With the workspace, follow along in your IDE.

To go further: [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd).

## 3. The R tutorial

**On the slides.** The tutorial puts R in one slide, then covers reading and inspecting the data, the verbs of datawizard that work on rows and columns, tables and tests, model formulas, a plot with tinyplot, causal graphs in R, and the error messages that you are most likely to meet. Type along in any cell of the browser lab, or in the console of your IDE.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

To go further: [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd).

## 4. Task 2 – The data

[Open the browser lab at Task 2](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-2-data){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

If you work in the workspace, use your report or `working_script.R` instead. Count the emails, the bounced ones, the delivered ones, the replies and the replies with a greeting code. Count the same for each group of names, with the share of the coded replies that greeted the sender by name, and draw that share for each of the six names. Then change one thing, such as counting by `name_sex` in place of `group`, and read what changes.

**By the end of the part** you can find your way around an IDE, read and write the R of the tutorial, and you have counted and drawn what came back for each of the six names: 1,014 emails, 23 bounced, 991 delivered, 563 replies and 558 replies with a greeting code.
